## Rulebook rules (Codex)

Codex reads this file instead of `AGENTS.md`; full rules: `AGENTS.md` and
`.rulebook/specs/`. The project rules below win on conflict.

- Per commit: type-check + lint + tests covering the change; before push/PR, the
  full suite, all green. Never bypass git hooks.
- Complete work, no stubs; root causes, not workarounds; surgical, simple diffs.
- Ask before destructive git (`reset --hard`, `checkout -- .`, `clean -f`,
  `push --force`, `rebase`, `stash`, `branch -D`) or deleting files. Never delete
  or move a `.git`; worktrees come out via `git worktree remove`.
- No OS schedules (cron, systemd, launchd, schtasks): scheduling lives in the app.
- Small, local work directly; delegate independent parts, broad exploration or
  long work — for context and parallelism, not speed.
- Multi-session work: rulebook tasks (`rulebook_task` MCP or `rulebook task`).
  CHANGELOG per PR/release.
- Rulebook's `.claude/hooks` guards don't run in Codex (project hooks need Codex
  trust and Codex tool names): these rules are the guard here.
<!-- RULEBOOK-CODEX:END -->

# Project-Specific Overrides

User-owned; survives `rulebook update`; wins on conflict.

- Execute requests end-to-end in one turn — no mid-task "should I proceed?"
  check-ins. Ask only for genuine ambiguity that changes the outcome, or for
  destructive operations.
- Batch related work into few commits; report once at the end.
- Subagents and parallel dispatch are encouraged whenever work is parallel or
  context-heavy.
